Account managers can PATCH any deal by id; only stage-transition validity is checked, not that the deal is assigned to the acting account manager, so one AM can silently edit another AM's deals.

Decrypts an encrypted 'pipelineView' cookie (saved deal-pipeline filter state) using AES-256-CBC and distinguishes a padding failure ('bad decrypt') from other decryption errors via two different exception messages returned to the client, enabling a padding-oracle attack against the cookie.

Object.assign(deal, fields) merges the entire raw request body (Record<string, any>, no DTO/whitelist) onto the loaded Deal entity before saving, letting a caller overwrite any column (value, stage, assignedToId, organizationId) via PATCH /deals/:id/board-quick-edit.
Deal weighting preview builds a `new Function` from a user-supplied 'rule' query-string expression and executes it with `with(context)`, allowing arbitrary JS execution against the request.

Builds a raw SQL query by directly interpolating the uploaded file's originalName and mimeType (attacker-controlled multipart metadata) plus organizationId into a template string passed to docRepo.query(), called on every document upload to check for duplicates.
searchTerm is spliced unescaped into an XPath contains() expression, allowing XPath injection via crafted quotes/operators in the header value.
Unsanitized search term is written to the application log, allowing CRLF/log-forging injection of fake log lines.

Reachable via GET /escalations/:id/duplicate-chain. Recursively follows Escalation.duplicateOfId (settable via existing PATCH /escalations/:id, which forwards an arbitrary Partial<Escalation> dto straight into escalationRepo.update) with no depth counter and no cycle/visited-set check. An attacker who can update escalations can link A->B->...->A or build an arbitrarily long chain, causing unbounded recursive DB lookups / stack growth per request.

A support-agent-facing quick-reply preview endpoint joins an attacker-controlled JSON body field (templateName) directly into a filesystem path and reads it with fs.readFileSync, allowing path traversal (e.g. '../../etc/passwd' or reading other server files) since no basename/sanitization is applied.
Resumes an on-call case handoff by trusting jwt.decode() claims (escalationId/responderId) with no signature verification at all; any forged/tampered assertion is accepted.
Stores an uploaded case attachment to the web-served public directory using the client-supplied original filename, with no MIME type or size validation.
Reads a case attachment by joining an unsanitized fileName param onto CASE_ATTACHMENTS_PUBLIC_DIR with no traversal check, allowing ../ escapes.
reportLabel from the URL is joined into a filesystem path and written with fs.writeFileSync with no basename/allowlist check.

Board-packet PDF rendering shells out to pandoc via execSync with a template literal built from the user-supplied 'layout' query param (?layout=...), reachable via GET /exports/:reportLabel/board-packet, allowing arbitrary shell command injection.

Uploaded JSON organization-backup snapshot is JSON.parse'd and Object.assign'd directly onto the loaded ORM entity, then saved — unvalidated mass assignment of arbitrary fields (including ones not on any DTO) into the organization record.

Billing-standing lookup: when the client passes ?supportContext=integration-console, the 502 error response includes err.stack and the raw query context; the flag is fully client-controlled with no auth/env gate.
Third-party API failure details (message + stack) are leaked verbatim to the API client instead of being logged server-side with a generic response.
After a legacy partner-tier rebate handoff, the controller redirects to a fully client-supplied continueUrl query parameter with no allowlist or same-origin check.
Returns the full TypeORM User entity (including the bcrypt password hash column) directly as the HTTP response body for the internal team-directory lookup, with no DTO projection or field exclusion.

A customer contact can set the cookie manually and read delivery payloads for webhooks belonging to other organizations.
